title: Cross-Reference Intelligence Findings
methodology: Algorithmic cross-referencing of 5 government datasets: OpenParliament (151 bills, 94 votes, 340 MPs), Commissioner of Lobbying (547K contacts), Elections Canada (6.2M contributions), CRA charity filings, and open.canada.ca procurement (3,133 contracts). They directly lobbied the PMO 186 times including PM Trudeau 15 times personally.

finding_9_ethics_enforcement_failure.title: Ethics Enforcement Failure — Zero Consequences for 9 Violations
finding_9_ethics_enforcement_failure.summary: The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner has found at least 9 sitting or former ministers and officials guilty of violating the Conflict of Interest Act since 2017. In every case, the penalty was ZERO — no fines, no criminal referral, no removal from office. PM Trudeau was found guilty TWICE (Aga Khan 2017 — 4 sections violated; SNC-Lavalin 2019 — s.9 violated). Finance Minister Morneau violated 3 provisions (WE Charity). Minister LeBlanc awarded a clam licence to his wife's cousin. Minister Ng gave contracts to a personal friend. Speaker Fergus violated the act he was supposed to enforce. SDTC Board Chair Verschuren voted on grants to her own company NRStor. The Ethics Commissioner has NO enforcement mechanism — findings are published and ignored. This structural failure is the single strongest argument for Criminal Code s.122 (Breach of Trust) prosecution reform.

evidence.fact: PM Trudeau: 4 sections violated (Aga Khan, 2017) + s.9 violated (SNC-Lavalin, 2019). Penalty: zero.
evidence.source: Ethics Commissioner — Trudeau Report I + Trudeau Report II

evidence.fact: Finance Minister Morneau: 3 provisions violated (WE Charity — s.6(1), s.7, s.21). Daughter employed by WE during $900M contract. Penalty: zero.
Minister LeBlanc: s.6(1) and s.21 violated (Arctic surf clam licence to wife's cousin). His sister-in-law was interim Ethics Commissioner (Marguerite Legault).
Minister Ng: s.6(1) and s.21 violated ($22K in contracts to personal friend's PR firm, 20-year friendship).
Speaker Fergus: Violated Conflict of Interest Act by writing CRTC support letter.
SDTC Chair Verschuren: s.6(1) and s.21 violated — voted on grants to her OWN company NRStor ($217K). AG found 186 board conflicts across $400M.
evidence.source: Ethics Commissioner — Verschuren Report + AG Report

evidence.fact: Randy Boissonnault: Under ethics investigation for business dealings while in cabinet. Fake Indigenous identity on government contract bids. Police investigating.
Yasmin Ratansi: Employed foster sister with fake name on business cards. Ordered to repay $9,391.
Dean Del Mastro (CPC): ONLY federal MP convicted of election fraud — 1 month prison. Shows that criminal prosecution IS possible when applied.

finding_9_ethics_enforcement_failure.pattern: 9 violations, zero penalties. The Ethics Commissioner publishes reports that are universally ignored. The structural problem: the Act has no enforcement mechanism. The solution: Criminal Code s.122 (Breach of Trust by Public Officer — up to 5 years imprisonment) must be actively prosecuted when the Ethics Commissioner finds a violation.
finding_9_ethics_enforcement_failure.key_stat: 9 ethics violations across 2 prime ministers, 4 ministers, 1 Speaker, 1 board chair, and 2 MPs — combined penalty: $9,391 (Ratansi repayment). No fines, no criminal referrals, no removals.
